answer: Use rate-limiting nullifiers. Each identity stakes a deposit and commits to a secret; every vote carries a zero-knowledge proof plus one share of that secret, bound to the epoch. One vote per epoch reveals nothing, but a second leaks another share, so anyone can rebuild the secret and claim the deposit. An operator who reuses one bonded key to echo forty verdicts on a canyon flood survey is slashed on the second vote, so each extra voice needs its own stake, while an agent counting sparrow nests votes once and stays anonymous.
